outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms associated with damaging wind gusts and hail are likely today across parts of the Carolinas into the Middle Atlantic and Southeast. Isolated severe storms may also develop across parts of the Great Plains and Mid Missouri Valley.

sections.title: Eastern States
sections.text: An upper-level trough will move eastward from the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys across the Southern and Central Appalachians into the Carolinas today. Ahead of the trough, a moist airmass will be in place from Georgia northeastward across the Carolinas into the Mid-Atlantic with surface dewpoints in the upper 60s and lower 70s F. In response, a large corridor of moderate instability is forecast to develop from the southern Appalachian foothills eastward to the Atlantic coast. Thunderstorms appear likely to initiate and organize just ahead of the shortwave trough in the southern Appalachians around midday with this activity moving eastward into the foothills during the afternoon. Forecast soundings in the foothills in northwestern South Carolina and west-central North Carolina at 21Z show MLCAPE values reaching 2,000 J/kg with 0-6 km shear of 30-35 kt. This combined with veered southwesterly winds at the surface and westerly flow in the low to mid-levels will be favorable for quasi-linear development. As low-level lapse rates become steep in the afternoon, conditions will become favorable for wind damage along the leading edge of an MCS moving eastward away from the southern Appalachia

sections.title: Mid-Missouri Valley
sections.text: Westerly mid-level flow will be in place in the central U.S. today as a shortwave ridge develops across the central and northern Plains. Beneath the ridge, an axis of moderate to strong instability is forecast to develop ahead of a cold front from Kansas northward into the mid Missouri Valley. Convection appears likely to initiate along the front with thunderstorms moving eastward across parts of eastern Nebraska and western Iowa during the late afternoon. Forecast soundings at 21Z for Omaha, Nebraska and Kansas City, Missouri show MLCAPE reaching 2,500 J/kg and have strong deep-layer shear profiles. 0-6 km shear is forecast to be around 55 kt at both locations suggesting that supercells will be the likely storm mode. Convective coverage should remain relatively isolated due to a weak cap but any cells that can initiate and mature should have severe potential. The strong instability combined with steep low to mid-level lapse rates would be favorable for wind damage and large hail. A brief tornado would also be possible with supercells mainly during the early evening as low-level flow increases across the region.

sections.title: Central High Plains
sections.text: Mid-level flow is forecast to become west-southwesterly today across the central High Plains in the wake of a developing upper-level ridge in the mid Missouri Valley. At the surface, backed east-southeasterly flow will be in place which will reinforce an axis of moisture and instability from southern Kansas extending northwestward into northeastern Colorado and western Nebraska. As surface temperatures warm, convection will initiate in the higher terrain of northeastern Colorado and spread eastward into the central High Plains this afternoon. Steep low to mid-level lapse rates and moderate to strong deep-layer shear, evident on forecast soundings, will be favorable for severe storms. Dry air in the low-levels may contribute to downburst potential but isolated large hail will be possible especially if a supercell can develop. ..Broyles/Squitieri.. 06/20/2019

outlooks.summary: Swaths of damaging winds are most likely from southern Virginia to eastern Georgia this afternoon. The risk for very large hail with a few tornadoes exists across parts of the Mid-Missouri Valley this afternoon into early evening. Otherwise, scattered severe storms are expected across a broad portion of the central and northern Great Plains, and over the eastern states.

sections.title: Carolinas and VA
sections.text: Primary change is to expand the Enhanced Slight Risk and further increase wind probabilities. Shortwave trough over the TN Valley will reach the Mid-Atlantic States this evening. Attendant belt of strong 700-500 mb southwesterlies (45-55 kt) will overspread much of the Piedmont and Coastal Plain downstream of this trough. Remnant convective clusters are ongoing just ahead of the trough across the southern Appalachians and the other near the trough axis over central AL. Renewed convective vigor is expected towards midday as downstream destabilization occurs of an air mass characterized by low 70s surface dew points. Multiple MCSs should develop during the afternoon with steep low-level lapse rates supporting a primary threat for several swaths of wind damage.

sections.title: Lower Missouri Valley
sections.text: Primary changes are expand Slight Risk and to increase probabilities for very large hail and tornadoes. A lead shortwave trough over central SD will track into IA by afternoon. This feature is supporting ongoing non-severe convection from eastern SD to the KS/NE border. In the wake of this activity, most CAMs suggest potential for at least one long-track supercell developing southeast along an intensifying baroclinic zone/instability gradient. 50-60 kt 500-mb westerlies amid strong speed shear between 700-300 mb will yield an elongated hodograph favorable for potentially a long-track swath of large hail, some of which could be significant. However, uncertainties exist to preclude an upgrade in categorical risk. One is the expansiveness of the ongoing elevated convection and related slowing of boundary-layer destabilization. Another is the tendency for guidance to be too aggressive in boundary-layer moisture return given that upper 60s surface dew points are currently relegated to OK south. But as boundary-layer moisture increases from the south, the tornado risk should maximize during the late afternoon to early evening along/near the cool side of the baroclinic zone. Rising mid-le

sections.title: Northern/central High Plains
sections.text: Primary change is to expand Slight Risk. Amplification of the large-scale upper trough is expected as a vigorous shortwave impulse and associated speed max dig across the Pacific Northwest to the northern Rockies by evening. This will induce a sharpening lee trough across eastern portions of CO/WY/MT, yielding an increase in low-level upslope flow and moisture return from lower elevations during the evening. Scattered thunderstorms will develop along the trough during the late afternoon and are expected to be initially high-based off the Front Range. The surge in low-level moisture should sustain convection across the central High Plains and yield clusters continuing tonight into parts of NE/KS. Severe hail and wind along with a brief tornado are possible. Farther north across southeast MT and vicinity, large-scale ascent will be stronger and hodographs will be impressively elongated owing to its proximity to the amplifying shortwave impulse. This should offset a cooler boundary-layer with more meager buoyancy to sustain a risk for a few supercells with hail/tornado being the main hazards. ..Grams/Gleason.. 06/20/2019

outlooks.summary: Swaths of damaging winds are most likely from southern Virginia to eastern Georgia this afternoon. The risk for very large hail with a few tornadoes exists across parts of the Mid-Missouri Valley this afternoon into early evening. Otherwise, scattered severe storms are expected across a broad portion of the central and northern Great Plains, and over the eastern states.

sections.title: Southeast and Mid Atlantic States
sections.text: A progressive shortwave trough is evident in morning water vapor imagery over AL, with other minor MCVs farther north over east TN and WV. These features will track eastward today across much of the Southeast states and Mid Atlantic region. Strong daytime heating is occurring over this region, where dewpoints in the 70s will yield afternoon MLCAPE values of 1000-2000 J/kg. Strong westerly flow aloft, steep low-level lapse rates, and favorable large-scale forcing will combine for an active strong/severe thunderstorm event for this region. Multiple lines and clusters of storms will traverse the area this afternoon and evening, posing a risk of damaging winds and some hail.

sections.title: Northern PA/NJ/NY into New England
sections.text: Persistent cloud cover is limiting heating/destabilization from northern PA/NJ northward into New England. Despite the limited thermodynamic environment, model guidance and recent radar trends suggest the potential for scattered afternoon thunderstorms. Forecast soundings show very favorable vertical shear profiles for organized or even rotating storms capable of gusty winds and perhaps a tornado. However, given the weak CAPE profiles, it appears that the severe risk in this area will remain widely spaced and primarily marginal. Nevertheless, have extended the SLGT risk area northward into central NY ahead of ongoing strong activity.

sections.title: NE/IA/KS/MO
sections.text: A well-defined shortwave trough is moving across SD/NE this morning. 12z model guidance provides continued confidence that a cluster of intense storms will continue to develop/evolve with this feature over northeast NE and track southeastward into parts of IA/MO/KS. These storms may produce very large hail and damaging winds. This corridor may require an upgrade to ENH at 20z once mesoscale details become more clear on the evolution of the cluster of storms.

sections.title: Northern and Central High Plains
sections.text: Strong heating is occurring today from southeast MT into eastern WY and far eastern CO, where dewpoints in the mid 40s to lower 50s and steep mid-level lapse rates are present. Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop along this axis by mid/late afternoon - spreading eastward through the evening. Forecast soundings show favorable vertical shear profiles for a few supercells capable of large hail and damaging winds. An isolated tornado or two is also possible. The activity which forms in eastern CO/western KS appears to have the best chance of persisting deep into the evening and spreading farther east across KS. ..Hart/Jirak.. 06/20/2019

outlooks.summary: Damaging wind risk continues from southern Virginia to eastern Georgia this afternoon. The risk for very large hail with a few tornadoes also persists across parts of the Mid-Missouri Valley this afternoon into early evening. Otherwise, scattered severe storms are expected across a broad portion of the central and northern Great Plains, and over the eastern states.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: No substantive changes are being made to the ongoing outlook, as forecast reasoning, and general areas of greater risk, remain on track. The greatest change to the existing areas is a decrease in the expanse of both the MRGL risk area and thunder area over the southern Plains, where capping is expected to largely hinder convective risk. Otherwise, severe risk continues over portions of the Southeast, where ongoing watches and warnings are in effect. Meanwhile, severe storms are expected to develop from the central and northern high Plains eastward across the central Plains region later this afternoon and evening. ..Broyles.. 06/20/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1116 AM CDT Thu Jun 20 2019/

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms associated with a wind damage threat will continue for a few more hours this evening across parts of the Southeast. Large hail, wind damage and a couple brief tornadoes will be possible across parts of the Great Plains and Mid Missouri Valley through tonight.

sections.title: Southeast/Eastern Carolinas
sections.text: A linear MCS located from eastern North Carolina southwestward into southern Georgia will continue to move southeastward across moderately unstable airmass this evening. Steep low-level lapse rates and moderate deep-layer shear will support a wind damage threat with the stronger parts of the lines. The wind damage threat will be maximized with the faster moving sections of the line and along the leading edge of bowing segments. The wind damage threat should persist the longest across far southern Georgia in northeast Florida where MLCAPE values are estimated to be in the 2000 to 3000 J/kg range. For this reason, a small enhanced risk is maintained from southern Georgia into northeastern Florida.

sections.title: Central and Northern Plains/Mid Missouri Valley
sections.text: The latest water vapor imagery shows an upper-level ridge over the central Plains with west to southwest mid-level flow over the High Plains. At the surface, a 999 mb low is located in southeast Wyoming with upslope east-southeasterly flow located across much of Nebraska and western Kansas. In response, a corridor of strong instability is present across west-central Kansas where the RAP is estimating MLCAPE values in the 4000 to 5000 J/kg range. Further to the northwest, strong to severe thunderstorms have developed along the western edge of moderate instability from western Nebraska into northeastern Colorado. These thunderstorms will continue to move eastward into stronger instability. Moderate to strong deep-layer shear along with steep mid-level lapse rates will be favorable for supercells with large hail. The more dominant supercells may produce hailstones of greater than 2 inches in diameter. The greatest chance for very large hail will be along the northern edge of the strongest instability from northern Kansas into southeast Nebraska, northwestern Missouri and southwest Iowa. sections.title: Southern Minnesota/Western Iowa/Northeast Kansas
sections.text: The latest radar imagery shows a few isolated severe thunderstorms located along an axis of moderate instability across the mid Missouri Valley extending north-northeastward into the Upper Mississippi Valley. MLCAPE values are estimated by the RAP in the 1500 to 3000 J/kg range which is confirmed by the Omaha and Kansas City 00Z soundings. In addition, the soundings have 0-6 km shear of 40-50 kt suggesting the environment will continue to support supercell development this evening. Large hail, wind damage and a brief tornado or two will be possible. Later this evening into the overnight period, a linear MCS with embedded supercells and bowing line segments will move into the region from the west. This will maintain an isolated tornado threat along with potential for large hail and wind damage. ..Broyles.. 06/21/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Elevated convection across northern Nebraska this morning continues to persist and move into a more favorable environment. Trends will continue to be monitored for a possible watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: In the wake of overnight/early morning convection supported by warm air advection across the mid-Missouri Valley, a favorable corridor for supporting severe weather is developing across eastern Nebraska. A lead shortwave trough evident in water vapor imagery is moving across northern Nebraska this morning aiding in convective development. If thunderstorms are able to persist as they move to the southeast, they will encounter an environment characterized by MUCAPE over 1000 J/kg and effective bulk shear over 50 knots, clearly supportive of organized convection. Most CAM guidance suggests that one or two long-lived supercells will evolve out of this activity and move south-southeast near the Nebraska-Iowa border. The primary severe weather threat from these storms will likely be large hail, but as the storms become rooted in the boundary layer over time, isolated damaging wind gusts and a tornado or two will be possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to develop by 17-18Z over a large part of the Southeast U.S. and increase in coverage and intensity during the afternoon, posing a risk for damaging wind and hail. A WW will probably be needed for a portion of this region by 17Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A moist warm sector resides over a large part of the southeast U.S. with dewpoints around 70F and temperatures climbing through the mid 80s F as of 16Z. Latest objective analysis indicate MLCAPE around 1500-2000 J/kg and further destabilization will occur as the surface layer continues to warm. Water vapor imagery shows a progressive shortwave trough moving through the TN Valley, with an MCV also indicated over southeast TN/northern GA. A low-level confluence zone is forecast to evolve well inland from the coast from southern AL through southern GA. The combination of forcing for ascent associated with the MCV and progressive shortwave trough, surface layer destabilization and subtle boundaries, should promote warm sector initiation by early afternoon. While deep-layer wind profiles are unidirectional west southwesterly with small 0-1 km hodographs, a belt of 50 kt mid-level winds within the base of the trough is resulting in 30-35 kt effective bulk shear. This environment should support both multicell and some supercell structures with discrete modes eventually evolving into lines and clusters capable of damaging wind and hail.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to develop during the early afternoon posing a risk for damaging wind and hail. A severe thunderstorm watch will probably be needed by 18-19Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The warm sector continues to destabilize over a large part of the Mid Atlantic region from North Carolina through VA and MD. Surface dewpoints around 70F and temperatures warming through the mid to upper 80s have boosted MLCAPE to 1500-2000 J/kg. WV imagery shows the primary shortwave trough over the TN Valley, but with an MCV moving through the southern Appalachians. These features are progressive, and the accompanying forcing for ascent along with boundary layer destabilization should result in an increase in thunderstorm coverage and intensity this afternoon. Wind profiles are unidirectional west southwesterly with 30-40 kt deep-layer flow, but modest 0-6 km shear generally less than 35 kt. This environment will support mostly multicell modes, but mid-level updraft rotation will also be possible in some storms. Activity may evolve into clusters and line segments with time posing a risk for damaging wind and hail through the afternoon into early evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage and intensity this afternoon ahead of an approaching shortwave trough. The strongest storms will primarily pose a threat of damaging wind gusts, and trends will be monitored for the necessity of a watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Despite developing in an environment with limited instability, thunderstorms across central New York have shown some signs of organization, likely aided by the convectively enhanced midlevel circulation moving across northern New York. Ahead of this convection into far south-central New York and eastern Pennsylvania, visible satellite imagery indicates pockets of heating allowing for some destabilization. As such, additional warm sector thunderstorms are expected to develop, and given the sufficient deep-layer shear, there will be some potential for organized storm modes. These storms would primarily pose a damaging wind threat through the afternoon and early evening hours. At this time, there is uncertainty whether storm coverage and intensity will necessitate watch issuance, but convective trends will be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms may produce a few instances of hail and strong wind gusts from middle through northeast Tennessee into southeast Kentucky next couple hours. The duration and overall magnitude of the threat is not expected to be sufficient for a WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms are developing from southeast KY into northern middle TN along and east of a cold front and in association with ascent attending a progressive shortwave trough. Extensive morning clouds were slow to erode and have limited boundary layer recovery with temperatures still in the 70s F in most areas, limiting MLCAPE to generally below 1000 J/kg. A mid-level jet situated within the base of the trough is resulting in 35-40 kt effective bulk shear across TN, and some marginal supercell structures with modest mid-level updraft rotation have been observed. Activity will continue east southeast next couple hours, posing some risk for locally strong wind gusts and hail. However, storms should begin a weakening trend by 22Z as they encounter a more stable boundary layer toward the southern Appalachians.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for scattered damaging wind and some hail will persist from southern Georgia through the eastern Carolinas and eastern Virginia through early evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Numerous storms have developed in the moist, weakly capped and moderately unstable warm sector this afternoon. Some discrete modes still exist, but trends should be for more storms to evolve into line segments and clusters. A mid-level 40-50 kt jet within the base of a progressive upper trough is resulting in 30-40 kt unidirectional effective bulk shear, so some storms may develop mid-level updraft rotation. Activity is expected to remain strong to severe as it continues toward the coast next couple hours. ..Dial.. 06/20/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms developing over the higher terrain are beginning to move eastward onto the plains. Convective trends will be monitored regarding the need for a possible watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Despite modest low-level moisture across Colorado, strong heating has led to destabilization and thunderstorm development over the higher terrain. Westerly midlevel flow around 30-40 knots (per area VWPs) is promoting eastward movement of these high-based thunderstorms toward the plains. Given the low-level easterly upslope component of the flow, deep-layer shear (over 40 knots) will be sufficient for organized storm structures and a damaging wind and hail threat. While limited moisture/instability may hinder storm strength/severity initially, as the storms move eastward into better moisture, the intensity of storms are expected to increase. Furthermore, storm cold pool mergers and an increasing low-level jet this evening should promote upscale growth with time, enhancing severe wind potential. Convective trends will be monitored for the possibility of a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong thunderstorms are beginning to develop over southeast MT. A watch may be needed in the next hour.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms have begun to form over southeast MT in the past hour. This appears to be associated with weak low-level upslope flow into higher terrain, as well as increasing ascent as a strong shortwave trough over ID digs eastward. Forecast soundings in this area show rather meager CAPE values with dewpoints in the 30s and lower 40s. However, vertical shear profiles are moderately strong with straight-line hodographs. Present indications are that a few severe storms and perhaps supercells will form in this region this afternoon - spreading eastward through the evening. Large hail is likely the main threat. A WW may be needed relatively soon for this area. ..Hart.. 06/20/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms persists across Redwood/Brown counties currently. A WW is being considered, and trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms in the discussion area have evolved into a small cluster of semi-discrete cells. These storms are in an environment characterized by moderate instability and relatively weak low-level shear, though it appears that cells have recently favorably interacted with a warm front/stationary boundary in the region and acquired occasional updraft rotation. This has results in occasional instances of large hail, funnel clouds, and even a brief tornado within the past 15 minutes or so. Storms have also taken on a rightward-moving component as well, with updraft motion along the boundary suggestive of possible persistence toward the MN/IA border through the evening. Given these trends, a WW issuance may be needed especially if storms maintain their intensity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues to shift quickly eastward across portions of North Carolina and South Carolina, while shifting more slowly southward across southern Georgia/southeastern Alabama.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Damaging wind gusts continue to be the primary threat with ongoing storms, which have generally congealed into elongated linear bands from eastern North Carolina southwestward to southwestern Georgia. The pre-convective environment remains moderate to strongly unstable, with strong deep shear (resulting from 40-kt mid-level flow) continuing to support storm/linear organization. Storms have reached coastal waters in eastern SC/NC over the past half hour, resulting in a diminished severe threat in adjacent upstream areas. Meanwhile in southern Georgia, southern South Carolina, and vicinity, storms are taking on more of a southeastward component to motion and will spread through remaining portions of WWs 408 and 410 through the remainder of the evening. Behind this linear complex, convective overturning has stabilized the low-levels, and attendant portions of WWs 408 and 409 can be canceled early. Farther west into Alabama, storms have generally struggled to reach severe thresholds - probably being due to displacement from stronger lift/ascent aloft compared to areas northeast and weaker surface convergence. Should convective trends dictate, portions of WW 410 in southeast Alabama may also be canceled early. ..Cook.. 06/20/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Short-term convective trends will be monitored for sustained thunderstorm development. A small watch may need to be considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery during the past 30 minutes is showing rapid convective development with a discrete updraft over northeast KS. Surface temperatures in northeast KS are near 90 degrees F with upper 60s dewpoints. Recent runs of the HRRR are void of thunderstorm development over northeast KS which may be explained in part by weak 12hour 500mb height rises over the lower-mid MO Valley. The 00z Topeka raob showed a very unstable airmass (around 3500 J/kg MLCAPE) with 40kt effective shear---conditionally supportive of supercell development. However, relatively subdued flow in the lowest few km may limit low-level mesocyclone development and a conditional risk for a tornado. Nonetheless, if a storm can become rooted in the boundary layer, large to very large hail and severe gusts are possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Upscale growth into one or more clusters of storms is expected across the southern NE/northern KS region this evening into the overnight. The severe threat will likely transition to mainly a concern for wind gusts. The large hail risk will likely become increasingly confined to more discrete or supercellular storm modes during the evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic over the central High Plains shows a couple of quasi-discrete thunderstorm clusters from northeast CO northward into the NE Panhandle. Recent subjective surface analysis places a maritime warm front arcing from near Garden City, KS northeastward into southeast NE with surface dewpoints around 70 degrees F south of the boundary. To the north of the boundary over northwest KS and southwest NE, a drier airmass with upper 50s dewpoints was sampled by the 00z North Platte raob. Considerable mixed-layer convective inhibition was noted in the sounding (-200 J/kg) with a stout inversion around 700mb. A central Great Plains LLJ is forecast to intensify this evening with the terminus located over southern NE. Isentropic lift and low-level moist advection will focus over northern KS into the Platte River Valley. The expectation is for ongoing severe activity over the northern NE Panhandle to weaken by the late evening over northern NE due in part to boundary layer cooling and increasing convective inhibition becoming more hostile for thunderstorm development. However, farther south in closer proximity to increasingly rich low-level moisture, additional storm development is forecast early this evening as both warm air advection and moisture increase. Upscale growth into one or more eastward-moving clusters capable of severe gusts is expected near the NE/KS border. A new severe thunderstorm watch (perhaps partially replacing the tornado watch 411) will likely be needed within 1-2 hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat over the northern High Plains appears to have diminished substantially owing to boundary layer stabilization. The severe thunderstorm watch will probably be canceled early prior to the 05z expiration time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a storm near the Treasure/Rosebud county border in southeast MT with other weak thunderstorms near the MT/SD border. Temperatures have cooled into the lower 60s over southeast MT and vicinity and this has resulted in weakening surface-based instability. Although large-scale upper forcing for ascent will gradually strengthen this evening, it appears both the detrimental effects of some convective overturning combined with cooling temperatures has yielded weaker storms and a diminished severe risk. ..Smith.. 06/21/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for strong wind gust will continue across south-central NE and north-central KS for the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Ongoing MCS along the central KS/NE border has shown a notable forward surge in last half hour or so. Current storm motion is eastward at 44 kt. Several wind gusts of 70-75 mph have been reported across Furnas County Nebraska where this forward surge occurred. Reflectivity aloft has since decreased slightly and the some weakening of the low-level reflectivity has been noted. Persistence of this well-organized MCS is anticipated for at least the next several hours, but the overall intensity (and resulting strength of the wind gusts) is uncertain, particularly given the reflectivity trends previously noted. That being said, the downstream air mass is characterized by very strong buoyancy (almost 7000 J/kg of MLCAPE on the 02Z LMN sounding) and 30 to 40 kt of effective bulk shear, both of which are more than supportive of storm persistence. Given the recent trends, the threat for strong wind gusts (i.e. 60 to 70 mph) will likely persist for the next few hours, although the likelihood of significant wind gusts (i.e. 75+ mph) appears to be lowering. ..Mosier.. 06/21/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for damaging wind gusts will likely persist and a watch will likely be needed downstream of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 413.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent storm motion of the ongoing MCS currently over south-central NE/north-central KS was estimated at eastward/northeastward at 45 kt. This motion takes it to the edge of Severe Thunderstorm Watch by 413 by 08Z. Temperatures and dewpoints gradually decrease with eastward/northeastward extent into southwest IA/northwest MO but, given the very steep lapse rates, remain sufficient for moderate to strong buoyancy. This buoyancy, coupled with the well-organized character of the ongoing MCS and adequate deep-layer vertical shear, suggest the potential for damaging wind gusts will continue eastward into far eastern NE, far northeast KS, far northwest MO, and southwest IA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for damaging wind gusts and occasional hail continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watches 413 and 414.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MCS which moved through south-central NE/north-central KS earlier has now reached the NE/IA border along its more progressive northern end. This portion of the system has shown significant weakening over the past hour or so as it encounters less favorable low-level moisture and slightly cooler temperatures. Southern portion of the line over northeast KS remains progressive, but less so than the northern end, with some backbuilding recently observed. A sharp reflectivity gradient still exists over this portion of the line and the downstream air mass is warm, moist, and highly buoyant. This portion of the line currently exhibits the largest threat for damaging wind gusts. Isolated hail is also possible. Farther west, initially discrete storms developing within the warm-air advection regime along the cold pool of the preceding MCS have organized into another forward-propagating system. Current trends suggest this MCS is elevated above the cold pool and no severe wind gusts have been reported thus far. Downstream air mass is very moist and buoyant, and there is some potential for strong wind gusts to begin reaching the surface. ..Mosier.. 06/21/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
